svg.aria-label: Four stages of channel formation in a 1 km mineral-filled network with six braided paths. Stage 1: pore space opens near the inlet while flow still crosses filled fractures, so PR_pore falls while PR_V holds. Stage 2: the front runs down the two inherited high-flow paths. Stage 3: one open path reaches the outlet and carries most of the flow; PR_V is at its minimum and PR_pore is back up. Stage 4: neighbouring paths open, flow spreads and both measures recover.
svg.text: 1 · pore space opens near the inlet
flow still crosses filled fractures: PRpore falls, PRV holds
2 · the front runs down inherited paths
the two initial high-flow paths open far downstream
one open path reaches the outlet and takes most of the flow
neighbouring paths open, flow spreads again: both recover
PRV: flow spread relative to fracture volume · PRpore: relative to open pore volume (1 = flow proportional to that volume; low = flow concentrated away from it)
